title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CURTIS AND HIS DAD
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Curtis Bell, a delivery driver from Little Rock, Arkansas.
His dad Leon, eighty-one, backed his Buick into the same mailbox three times.
So Curtis took the keys, and moved his dad into the spare room. Two stubborn men. One bathroom.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE EGGS
segments.quote: We shall sooner have the fowl by hatching the egg than by smashing it.
segments.author: Abraham Lincoln
lines: Every morning, Curtis rushed. Shoes on, coat on, let's go, Dad.
One day Leon dropped a whole carton of eggs.
He laughed, and quoted Abraham Lincoln:
We shall sooner have the fowl by hatching the egg than by smashing it.
Curtis set his alarm twenty minutes earlier. Now they ate breakfast on the porch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CHAIR
segments.quote: Do not let what you cannot do interfere with what you can do.
segments.author: John Wooden
lines: But Leon just sat by the window. Can't drive. Can't stand all day.
Curtis thought of the sign at his gym, from coach John Wooden:
Do not let what you cannot do interfere with what you can do.
But Leon, a barber for fifty years, could still cut hair.
So Curtis bought an old barber chair for forty dollars, and put it on the porch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: MR. PRUITT
segments.quote: There is no charm equal to tenderness of heart.
segments.author: Jane Austen
lines: Soon, neighbors lined up on the steps.
Mr. Pruitt, who had about nine hairs left, got a full hour.
Leon showed Curtis Mom's old copy of Emma, by Jane Austen:
There is no charm equal to tenderness of heart.
So Curtis learned the names on his route. Mr. Pruitt got a seat at Sunday supper.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE MIRROR
segments.quote: Wrinkles should merely indicate where smiles have been.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: Then Curtis took a turn in the chair. Gray hair, big frown.
Leon tapped the comb and quoted Mark Twain:
Wrinkles should merely indicate where smiles have been.
Son, yours are all from frowning.
So when Leon signed them up for the State Fair rib contest, Curtis said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: The harder the conflict, the more glorious the triumph.
segments.author: Thomas Paine
lines: Contest day, a thunderstorm rolled in. The smoker went out.
Curtis wanted to quit. Leon, soaking wet, quoted Thomas Paine, the Revolution writer:
The harder the conflict, the more glorious the triumph.
They held a tarp, relit the coals, and finished with four minutes left.
Third place. The prize? A tire coupon. Leon said, keep it. I don't drive.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE CANDLES
segments.quote: No wise man ever wished to be younger.
segments.author: Jonathan Swift
lines: On Leon's eighty-second birthday, Curtis joked, want to be young again?
Leon blew out the candles and quoted the Irish writer Jonathan Swift:
No wise man ever wished to be younger.
Curtis stopped missing his quiet old life, and asked to learn the clippers.
The new porch sign says Bell and Son. Saturdays.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Slow down. Use what you've got. Be tender. Smile more. Keep going. Love your age.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Slow down. Use what you've got. Be tender. Smile. Keep going. Love your age.
I asked my barber to make me look younger. He polished my head.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
